implemented_capabilities.capability: Version-guarded atomic multi-entity commit (optimistic concurrency) in one Cypher query
implemented_capabilities.notes: commit() builds a single query: MATCH (gN {id:$g}) WHERE gN.version = $v for each guard, WITH *, then MERGE/SET of each node and MERGE of each edge, ending in RETURN 1. If any guard version differs, no row survives and nothing is written; the caller sees false. Node labels and relationship types are checked against closed allow-lists.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Memory supersession with automatic plan invalidation
implemented_capabilities.notes: migrate() creates a new Memory node with supersedes=<old id> and version old+1, marks the old node status='superseded' with supersededBy, links fresh -[:SUPERSEDES]-> old, clears incident.plan, rewinds the incident to stage 1 and re-queues the planning task, all in one guarded commit. Old memory is preserved, not deleted.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Approval gate that rejects stale plans
implemented_capabilities.notes: A plan records memoryIds and memoryVersions. On approve, planIsCurrent re-reads each cited memory and refuses if it is not status 'active' or its version differs, returning a 409 'plan uses outdated memory'. Stage 2 (apply) re-checks that the cited fact is still active and still names the same database.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Multi-agent staged workflow with task leases and hand-offs
implemented_capabilities.notes: Four stages (investigate, plan, apply, verify) handled by agents atlas, sage and echo as Task nodes with status/leaseUntil (60 s) claimed through a version-guarded write and linked HANDS_OFF_TO. Pause, resume and checkpoint events are persisted; each step guards the incident, the task and every memory it relied on, so a concurrent memory change aborts the step.

Native Cypher traversals over DEPENDS_ON|ROUTES_TO (variable length, head(collect(p)) shortest path per node), pattern comprehensions for active memories and root-cause incidents, shortestPath, full-text search via db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes, and algo.betweenness for critical services. Every tool returns the path steps that produced each hit.

After the simulated health check passes, writes an episodic Memory linked LEARNED_FROM the incident and HAS_MEMORY from the root-cause service, and bumps the procedure's verifiedRuns and lastVerifiedAt version so the next incident reuses it.

implemented_capabilities.capability: LLM reasoning client with deterministic fallback
implemented_capabilities.notes: Optional OpenAI Responses or Anthropic Messages tool-calling over a fixed read-only tool set; with no key it runs a deterministic policy over the same graph tools. The engine verifies the model's chosen procedure/fact are active memories and not in a forbidden list before building a plan, so model output cannot bypass memory state.

Recovery 'applies' a pool-size change to a field on the incident document and flips hard-coded after-metrics; four preset scenarios (pool, worker, cache, migration) and a fictional two-workspace seed (acme, orbit) are authored data. Nothing is executed against a real system.

graph_models_and_cypher: One graph per tenant: relayops_<tenant>. Labels: Service, Incident, Memory, Person, Team, Decision, Task, Event, Message. Relations (closed allow-list): DEPENDS_ON, ROUTES_TO, OWNS, MEMBER_OF, ON_CALL_FOR, RESOLVED, AFFECTS, ROOT_CAUSE, SIMILAR_TO, HAS_MEMORY, LEARNED_FROM, SUPERSEDES, ABOUT, MADE_BY, BASED_ON, HAS_EVENT, HAS_TASK, HAS_MESSAGE, HANDS_OFF_TO, USES. Each node stores id, kind, version, a full JSON payload and a set of lifted scalar properties. Notable Cypher: guarded multi-statement MERGE with WITH *; pattern comprehensions [(s)-[:DEPENDS_ON|ROUTES_TO*1..2]->(u:Service) | u]; head(collect(p)) after ORDER BY length(p); shortestPath((a)-[*..N]->(b)); db.idx.fulltext.queryNodes with a CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX; CALL algo.betweenness({nodeLabels, relationshipTypes}) (FalkorDB algorithm procedure, not Neo4j GDS). Memory nodes carry status (active, superseded) and version. No APOC.
algorithms: Optimistic-concurrency version guards on every write path (falkor.ts:commit, engine.ts guards arrays)
Supersession chain with status flip and SUPERSEDES edge (engine.ts:migrate)
Plan-currency check by re-reading cited memory id and version (engine.ts:planIsCurrent)
Reverse-dependency blast radius via variable-length DEPENDS_ON|ROUTES_TO paths (falkor.ts:blastRadius)
Suspect ranking: upstream services plus siblings sharing a dependency, ordered by depth and prior root-cause count (falkor.ts:suspects)
Full-text memory search with light stemming and prefix OR query (falkor.ts:searchMemory)
backend_interfaces: Express 5 (server/app.ts): GET /api/health, POST /api/session, GET /api/state, POST /api/model/check, POST /api/workspace, POST /api/incidents, GET /api/scenarios, GET /api/graph/:tool/:serviceId, GET /api/graph/critical, GET /api/graph/search, GET /api/graph/path, POST /api/incidents/:id/action (start|pause|resume|approve|migrate), POST /api/incidents/:id/messages, GET /api/export
frontend_interfaces: React single-page app src/App.tsx (3560 lines) with a d3-force ForceGraph.tsx graph view, incident timeline, shared-memory inspector, approval and evidence-correction controls, and a chat box
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: Shared graph memory with categories (semantic facts, procedural procedures, episodic outcomes) and statuses active or superseded; agents atlas, sage and echo hand work off through Task nodes (HANDS_OFF_TO) with leases; tool traces are persisted on events; decisions can forbid procedures; incident state machine open -> investigating -> awaiting_approval -> resolving -> resolved with paused and error states; evidence correction (migrate) supersedes a memory and invalidates the pending plan.
tests_present: 27 node:test cases (api 3, engine 9, graph 8, model 7) plus 2 Playwright specs. By default the tests run against an in-memory SQLite test double in tests/doubles.ts; npm run test:falkordb sets TEST_FALKORDB=1 to check that the Cypher matches the double. Not run by this audit.
security_findings: server/model.ts:320-345 and 396-420 - outbound fetch to api.openai.com and api.anthropic.com with keys from environment; fixed hosts, timeout 40 s; provider error bodies are deliberately not exposed to clients

server/falkor.ts:299,317,474,530,545 - depth, max and limit are interpolated into Cypher with template strings; callers pass numbers from code defaults (depth/max/limit), not from request input, and request-supplied ids go through parameters (low risk, but validate if exposed)
server/falkor.ts:160,174 - CREATE INDEX with labels and fields from constant lists (low risk)

server/app.ts:20-26 - session HMAC secret written to .data/session-secret with mode 0600; sessions are signed with timingSafeEqual and carry hard-coded memberships ['acme','orbit'] (line 33), so tenancy is demo-grade
server/app.ts:75-87 - local login is allowed from loopback without a code; remote use requires DEMO_ACCESS_CODE, compared with !== (not constant time)
server/app.ts:238 - /api/export returns every node and edge for the session tenant to any authenticated session
server/app.ts:45-60 - origin check on non-GET requests blocks cross-origin writes; JSON body limit 32 kb
No shell, eval or exec in the files read; no hard-coded secrets found
No LICENSE file: reuse rests on the user-attested owner permission
duplicates_or_overlaps: Incident root cause and blast radius (reverse DEPENDS_ON traversal), agent memory with handoffs, decision lineage, and above all supersession plus stale-plan invalidation, which is the core of an Evidence Drift Cascade. Overlaps with other incident/RCA repos on traversal and with agent-memory repos on task handoff.
evidence_drift_relevance: HIGH - explicit supersession (status superseded, supersededBy, SUPERSEDES edge, preserved history), version-pinned plan citations that fail approval when a cited memory changed, cascade that clears the dependent plan and re-queues planning, and write guards that abort an in-flight step if any memory it used changed.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: About 100 lines that together implement supersede-then-invalidate-dependent-plan with an approval gate that re-verifies cited evidence versions, backed by server/falkor.ts:FalkorStore.commit, a reusable single-query guarded write. This is the most direct existing model of the Evidence Drift Cascade in the audited set.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB (the guarded-commit Cypher is plain openCypher and ports to the Python client 1.8); TypeScript source must be re-implemented in Python; LLM keys optional

strategy_rationale: The supersession, version-guarded commit and stale-plan approval gate are domain-neutral and should be re-implemented in Python as a shared evidence-lifecycle engine, using this repo as the behavioral spec and tests/engine.test.ts as acceptance cases. The incident simulation, seed data and UI are not worth importing.
